label: conj:hecke-anyonic-substrate
title: Iwahori–Hecke algebra is the anyon algebra: every QOU particle is anyonic before observation
html:
Conjecture. Iwahori–Hecke algebra is the anyon algebra: every QOU particle is anyonic before observation

Conjecture (Iwahori–Hecke substrate is the anyon algebra). Let K be a closed braid representing a QOU particle. Let T_w \in H_n(R, q) be its Hecke normal form at a generic deformation parameter q. The topological statistics of K are governed by the braid group B_n acting on T_w via the surjection B_n \twoheadrightarrow H_n(R, q) defined by \sigma_i \mapsto T_{s_i} modulo the Hecke quadratic relation:

  (T_{s_i} - q)(T_{s_i} + 1) = 0.

Every particle in the substrate is an anyon [kitaev2006, nayak2008]. Exchanging two particles multiplies the wavefunction by a topological braiding matrix rather than a \pm 1 permutation sign. Bosonic and fermionic statistics are not fundamental. They emerge as the image of anyonic braiding under the observation functor \tau.

Algorithmic role. The reduction engine processes every transition as a braid-group element acting on H_n(R, q) via \sigma_i \mapsto T_{s_i}. No \pm 1 shortcuts exist at intermediate steps. At generic q, the braid matrices accumulate geometric information. Only the final trace under \tau collapses this data onto a \pm 1 statistic.

Conjectural status. The Schur–Weyl identification of H_n(q)-modules with anyon Hilbert spaces is classical. We conjecture that the entire particle spectrum of the substrate realizes exactly as H_n(R, q)-modules. No particle escapes the anyonic substrate prior to observation. Proving exhaustion requires the cyclotomic-KLR equivalence [khovanovlauda2009].
